verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/research/verify.py:134-140 - when deep.leading_token (deep.py:359-361, peels only *:-#>) is not a verdict word, the fallback substring-scans _AGREE_MARKERS (verify.py:109) over the whole line before looking for a standalone UNVERIFIED/DISAGREE token, so 'Verdict: UNVERIFIED - no source confirms ...', '[UNVERIFIED] ...', '1. UNVERIFIED - ...' parse as agree.
verdicts.acceptance_test: sidecar/tests/test_research_verify.py::test_parse_verdict_reads_a_labelled_verdict_word - assert _parse_verdict(s)[0]=='unverified' for 'Verdict: UNVERIFIED - no source confirms the 23% operating margin.', '**Verdict:** UNVERIFIED - no source confirms it.', 'Answer: UNVERIFIED - evidence does not support the figure.', '[UNVERIFIED] the sources do not confirm this.', 'The claim is UNVERIFIED; nothing I found confirms the 23% margin.', '1. UNVERIFIED - no source confirms'; 'Verdict: DISAGREE - sources agree on 21% not 23%' -> 'disagree'; 'Verdict: AGREE - reuters confirms' -> 'agree'; existing parse_verdict tests stay green.
verdicts.note: The entry's own repro holds at HEAD: all 3 proven UNVERIFIED strings plus the markdown variant return unverified. The verifier's labelled-verdict strings reproduce exactly (agree). This is the same llm-output-marker-scan defect class, left open by the fix shape's retained marker fallback, so it is partial, not a regression. Severity context: live llama3.1:8b with the real _verdict_for prompt led with the bare verdict word in 6 of 6 samples, and no live labelled verdict has been observed from any provider. HEAD moved 6741387b to 91dac548 mid-run with docs-only commits; the audited code is identical.

verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/research/finance.py:146 - _looks_like_ir uses host.startswith('investors.'/'investor.'/'ir.') without requiring the label to be a subdomain, so the bare registrable host investors.com (IBD news, after www. strip) is PRIMARY; finance.py:79-89 _IR_PLATFORM_DENYLIST omits github.io, wixsite.com, netlify.app, hubpages.com and matches blogspot only on .com, so ir.blogspot.in / investors.github.io / investors.wixsite.com / ir.netlify.app are PRIMARY.
verdicts.acceptance_test: sidecar/tests/test_research_finance.py::test_ir_host_prefix_never_promotes_news_or_platform_hosts - assert domain_tier(u) != TIER_PRIMARY for https://www.investors.com/news/technology/nvidia-stock-buy-now/, https://investors.github.io/pump, https://ir.blogspot.in/post, https://investors.wixsite.com/x, https://ir.netlify.app/x, https://investors.hubpages.com/x; assert rank_sources([IBD, GH, Reuters])[0].title == 'Reuters' and priority_note does not name them primary; controls ir.nvidia.com, investors.infosys.com, investor.apple.com, ir.tatamotors.com stay TIER_PRIMARY.
verdicts.note: The entry's own repro holds: Medium /investor-diary/ and WordPress /ir/ return 3, Reuters 2, rank_sources puts Reuters first, and priority_note shows only press. The verifier's cases reproduce exactly. With [Reuters, IBD, investors.github.io], rank_sources gives ['IBD','GH','Reuters'] and priority_note names [2, 3] as the primary record. That is the stated 'ir. host outranks Reuters' half of the entry. investors.com is a bug the fix introduced (the prefix matches the registrable name). ir.hotpennypicks.net (a registrant's own ir. subdomain) is the accepted ceiling of any host-prefix heuristic and is not counted.
